claims.text: The degree of chemical short-range order governs superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys.
Chemical short-range order modulates local lattice dynamics in high-entropy alloys.
Chemical short-range order modulates the electronic density of states.
Increasing chemical short-range order enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Increasing chemical short-range order reduces electron scattering caused by compositional disorder.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling and reduced disorder-induced electron scattering increase the superconducting transition temperature.
Controlled annealing or slow cooling can induce greater chemical short-range order while avoiding secondary-phase formation.
Rapid quenching retains a relatively high level of chemical disorder in the baseline alloy.
Chemical short-range order alters local lattice distortions.
Chemical short-range order alters the phonon spectrum or phonon density of states.
Enhanced chemical short-range order produces more uniform local bonding environments.
Samples with induced chemical short-range order will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than a random-alloy baseline.
Samples with induced chemical short-range order will have lower residual electrical resistivity than a random-alloy baseline.
Samples with induced chemical short-range order will have a sharper superconducting transition than a random-alloy baseline.
The proposed effect requires sufficient elemental lattice mobility to develop chemical short-range order without phase separation.
The proposed relationship is limited to systems in which electron-phonon coupling is the dominant pairing mechanism.
Alternative pairing mechanisms or significant magnetic interactions may prevent the proposed relationship from applying.
The cited refractory HfNbTaTiZr study found that increasing chemical short-range order modified the high-frequency phonon density of states.
The cited refractory HfNbTaTiZr study found that increasing chemical short-range order increased lattice thermal conductivity by about 12%.
Failure of higher measured short-range order to produce consistently higher Tc, lower residual resistivity, and a sharper transition would falsify the proposed mechanism.
